paper.title: Lower Bounds on Regret for Noisy Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Non-Bayesian GP bandit optimization, simple regret (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the optimization of a function $f$ defined on a compact domain $D = [0,1]^d$. ... we assume that the corresponding RKHS norm is bounded as $\|f\|_{k} \le B$. ... a noisy sample $y_t = f(x_t) + z_t$ is observed, with $z_t \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ ... Simple regret: At the end of $T$ rounds, an additional point $x^{(T)}$ is reported, and the simple regret incurred is $r^{(T)} = f(x^*) - f(x^{(T)})$.

settings.name_in_paper: Non-Bayesian GP bandit optimization, cumulative regret (lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the optimization of a function $f$ defined on a compact domain $D = [0,1]^d$. ... RKHS norm is bounded as $\|f\|_{k} \le B$ ... $z_t \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ ... Cumulative regret: At the end of $T$ rounds, the cumulative regret incurred is $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T r_t$, where $r_t = f(x^*) - f(x_t)$.

conditions: squared-exponential kernel k_SE with lengthscale l
algorithm must achieve E[r^(T)] <= epsilon for every f in F_k(B)

source.label: thm:instantaneous
source.quote: Fix $\epsilon \in \big(0,\frac{1}{2}\big)$, $B > 0$, and $T \in \ZZ$. Suppose there exists an algorithm that, for any $f \in \Fc_k(B)$, achieves an average simple regret $\EE[r^{(T)}] \le \epsilon$ after $T$ rounds. Then, provided that $\frac{\epsilon}{B}$ is sufficiently small, ... For $k = \kSE$, it is necessary that T = \Omega( \frac{\sigma^2}{\epsilon^2} (\log\frac{B}{\epsilon})^{d/2} ).

results.notes: RKHS norm bound B mapped to S. Bound is on the number of rounds needed for expected simple regret epsilon. Section on high probability notes analogous bounds hold with constant probability.

conditions: algorithm must achieve E[r^(T)] <= epsilon for every f in F_k(B)

source.label: thm:cumulative
source.quote: Fix $B > 0$ and $T \in \ZZ$. Suppose there exists an algorithm that, for any $f \in \Fc_k(B)$, achieves an average cumulative regret of $\EE[R_T]$ after $T$ rounds. Then ... For $k = \kSE$, it is necessary that \EE[R_T] = \Omega( \sqrt{T\sigma^2 (\log \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2} )^{d/2} } ) provided that $\frac{\sigma}{B} = O(\sqrt{T})$ with a sufficiently small implied constant.
